To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CLP converges when economies transit from developing to developed status.
the CLPs of developed and developing economies are different, and that real CLPs converge along the economic growth.

(i) the CLPs of developed and developing economies differ significantly in both nominal and real measurements; (ii) the real and nominal CLP of developing economies are significantly different; (iii) the real and the nominal CLPs of developed, upper middle income and low middle income economies are not significantly different; and (iv) the real CLPs are higher than the nominal CLPs in both developed and developing economies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the international comparison of CLP and the relationship between CLP and development status.
the measurement of CLP in a global context.
the CLP convergence of economies in the context of economic growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PPPs should be used in international CLP comparisons.
the PPP method should be used to compare CLP.
the CLPs of developed and developing countries are different in both nominal and real measurements, and that the real CLP of developing economies is always higher than the nominal CLP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CLPs converge as the economies grow.
the PPPs approach is a more appropriate means for international comparisons of CLP.
the real and nominal CLP of the same country are not the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PPPs approach is a more accurate method to measure CLP than the exchange rate approach.
CLP comparisons using PPP exchange rates are more accurate and reliable than nominal exchange rates.
the real and nominal CLP converge as the economy develops, and the CLP is a function of economic development.
